title: Factors and Highest Common Factor (HCF)
seo_title: Highest Common Factor (HCF) – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the factors of numbers from 1 to 99; identify common factors; find the highest common factor (HCF) of numbers. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on factors and the highest common factor (HCF): is it a factor, all the factors, factor pairs, common factors, HCF and HCF word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: HCF = biggest factor in both lists
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A factor divides a number exactly with no remainder. The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.
  • Find factors in pairs: 1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4.
  • A common factor divides both numbers. The highest common factor (HCF) is the biggest one.

Examples

Example

HCF of 18 and 24

18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18

24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24

Answer: 6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting 1 and the number itselfEvery number has 1 and itself as factors.
Giving the LCMThe HCF is never bigger than the smaller number.
Missing a factor pairCheck every number from 1 upwards.

faq.q: What is the HCF used for?
faq.a: To share things into equal groups and to reduce fractions to their lowest terms.
Yes, for numbers like 8 and 15 that share no other factor.
A number that divides another number exactly.
